deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a miscellaneous notebook. The previous page records a criterion of Weierstrass for extrema via Puiseux expansions. Page 53 opens a new topic: a definition aimed at a birationally (in fact biregularly) invariant discriminant for a one-parameter family of plane algebraic curves. The next page states the intended theorem D(y,x)=D(x,y), then retracts it ('wahrscheinlich garnicht richtig').

(1) Definition of an 'algebraischer Bund' B(y,x;κ). Start from a fixed irreducible equation F(x,y,κ)=0, where κ is a parameter (the 'k' of the transcription is the κ of the next page). The Bund is the totality of relations F'(x',y',κ)=0 obtained from F by transformations
  x' = R1(x,y,κ), y' = R2(x,y,κ)  with inverse  x = R3(x',y',κ), y = R4(x',y',κ),
where the R_i are rational functions. In modern terms this is an automorphism of the function field K = k(κ)(x,y) carrying the generator pair (x,y) to another generator pair (x',y').

(2) Two extra conditions:
- (a) The transformation is one-to-one ('umkehrbar eindeutig') at every point of the curve (Gebilde) F=0.
- (b) Finite points go to finite points.
Together these make the map an isomorphism of the affine curves, i.e. of the affine coordinate rings (a biregular, not merely birational, equivalence of the affine models over the parameter).

(3) Hilbert asserts ('d.h. mit andern Worten') that such transformations are exactly composites of two triangular steps:
- Step 1: y' = f(y,x,κ), with x kept. Here y' is rational in y, x, κ and is an integral ('ganze') algebraic function of x and κ, i.e. integral over k[κ,x]. So y is replaced by another integral primitive element of the same field over k(κ,x).
- Step 2: x' = g(x,y',κ), with y' kept. The next page adds: y is rational in x, y', κ, and x' is integral over k[κ,y'].
The struck words 'ferner x x+' are an abandoned phrasing.

(4) Purpose, from the next page.
- Form the discriminant of the field generated by y over k(κ,x). Hilbert calls it the 'Körper y'; it is evidently the discriminant of the integral closure of k[κ,x] in K, a polynomial in x and κ.
- Setting it to 0 defines a 'Körper x' whose discriminant is a polynomial in κ alone. Call this iterated discriminant D(y,x).
- Step 1 does not change the integral closure over k[κ,x], so D(y,x)=D(y',x).
- If moreover D(y,x)=D(x,y) (symmetry), then D is invariant under the Bund transformations and would be 'the discriminant of the Bund'.
- Hilbert begins a proof, then writes that these theorems are probably false.

My illustration: for F = y^2 - x^3 - κ the iterated polynomial discriminants, taken in both orders after reducing to squarefree parts, both give κ up to constants. This is consistent with the conjecture in this case, but polynomial (as opposed to field) discriminants are clearly not symmetric in general.
errors: The 'd.h. mit andern Worten' equivalence is asserted without proof. It is not clear that every biregular transformation of the affine curve over k[κ] factors as one triangular step in y (x fixed) followed by one triangular step in x (y' fixed). Even for automorphisms of the affine plane such a factorization needs arbitrarily many triangular steps (Jung–van der Kulk), so 'two successive steps' is at best a special case.

Condition (a), one-to-one at every point, is in tension with arbitrary singular models F=0. At singular points (nodes) a birational map need not be pointwise bijective, so the definition needs places (Stellen in the Riemann-surface sense) rather than points, which may be what 'Stelle' means.

The central claim D(y,x)=D(x,y), stated on the next page, is not established. Hilbert himself notes the Bund-discriminant theorems are 'probably not correct at all'. Iterated discriminants also depend on whether one takes polynomial discriminants, field discriminants, or radicals/squarefree parts. This page leaves that unspecified.
Minor slips: 'alge-grabischen' for 'algebraischen'; 'Tranformation'; missing commas in R(x'y'k); the verb 'ausführt' is missing after 'die Transformation ...'.

results.what: Definition of an equivalence class ('Bund') of plane curves F(x,y,κ)=0 depending on a parameter κ under rational, invertible transformations that are bijective on points and keep finite points finite (biregular equivalence of affine models over the parameter ring)
results.modern_name: Biregular/birational equivalence of affine curves over k[κ] (isomorphism of affine coordinate rings / integral models of a function field)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (birational classes, 1857); Kronecker 1881/82 and Dedekind–Weber 1882 (arithmetical theory of algebraic functions)

results.what: Claim that such transformations decompose into a triangular step y'=f(x,y,κ), integral over k[κ,x], followed by x'=g(x,y',κ)
results.modern_name: Triangular (de Jonquières-type) decomposition of polynomial/biregular maps
results.usually_credited_to: de Jonquières (1864) for plane Cremona; Jung (1942) and van der Kulk (1953) for affine plane automorphisms

results.what: Programme (continued on the next page) to define a birationally invariant iterated discriminant of a one-parameter family of curves via field discriminants, D(y,x)=D(x,y); abandoned as probably false
results.modern_name: Discriminant locus of a family of curves / iterated discriminants (Kronecker elimination theory)

deep.surprise_reason: These are notebook explorations in Kronecker's arithmetic theory of algebraic functions: a definition plus a conjectured invariance that Hilbert himself retracts on the next page. Interesting as a glimpse of young Hilbert working in the Kronecker tradition, but no new verified result.

checkable.asserts: The discriminant of F=y^2-x^3-κ with respect to y is 4(x^3+κ) (difference is 0).
The iterated discriminant in the order y then x is -6912κ^2, i.e. κ up to constants and powers (difference is 0).
The discriminant with respect to x is -27(κ-y^2)^2 (difference is 0).

The discriminant of the squarefree part with respect to y is 4κ. So in this example both orders give κ up to constants, consistent with D(y,x)=D(x,y) only after passing to squarefree parts (difference is 0).
Equals 0, so the naive iterated polynomial discriminant in the order x then y degenerates. Field (or squarefree) discriminants are needed for the claimed symmetry to make sense.
Equals 0: writing y = y' - x^2 (a step-1 transformation y' = y + x^2, integral over k[κ,x]) carries y^2-x^3-κ to y'^2-2x^2y'+x^4-x^3-κ.
Gives 4(x^3+κ), the same as before the step-1 transformation, illustrating D(y,x)=D(y',x).

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the manuscript reads 'alge-grabischen' (a slip for 'algebraischen'), not 'algegraischen'.
The parameter written 'k' is almost certainly κ (kappa), as on the next page.
Line 5: 'Tranformation' is as written; the intended word is 'Transformation'. A verb such as 'ausführt' is missing after the displayed formulas.
The R in the transformation formulas is a script/Fraktur ℜ (rational function), the same in all four formulas.
Second-to-last line: the whole phrase 'ferner x x+' is struck through; the text continues 'wo durch die erste Transformation statt y die neue Variable y' eingeführt [wird]'.
In step 2 the image reads x' = g(x, y', κ); likewise in the right-hand inverse formulas, x = ℜ(x', y', κ) and y = ℜ(x', y', κ).
